subject: SLA banding & concurrency mapping for Dedicated GPU pool - Sentinel
messages:
From: Alex Ramsey <alex.ramsey@sentinel.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@sentinel.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated commit — throughput & SLA bands (Sentinel)

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Sentinel is excited to move from pilot to a committed Dedicated pool, but before we lock numbers we need a clearer mapping from our workload to the GPU count and the SLA bands you offer. High level:
- Production start: Nov 1, initial live traffic ~750 reqs/minute (spiky).
- Typical request: chat-style completions, median prompt length 280 tokens, response ~120 tokens; 8% of requests are long-context (>=8k tokens).
- Peak concurrency observed during tests: ~380 concurrent active sessions (not all generating tokens at once).

Open questions for you:
1) What committed GPU count do you recommend for a 24/7 SLA at 99.5% (band A) vs a cost-optimized 95% band (band B)?
2) How do you bill burst overcommit (we expect short 3–5 minute spikes to ~1.5x baseline)?
3) Any discounts available if we agree to a 12-month reserved commit and commit to model quantization (8-bit)?

I've attached a small sample of request traces (sentinel_workload_sample.csv). Can you map this to a proposed pool size and an expected per-token cost for both SLA bands?

If easier, happy to run a short PoC with a baseline commit.

—Alex
Sentinel Inc — Head of Platform

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramsey <alex.ramsey@sentinel.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput & SLA bands (Sentinel)

Alex — thanks for the details and the traces. Quick read-through attached; high level recommendations below (keeping this readable for procurement):

Summary recommendation (short):
- Band A (99.5% SLA): 8x H100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) with 20% burst buffer capacity for short spikes.
- Band B (95% SLA, cost-optimized): 5x H100-equivalent GPUs, with optional pay-as-you-go burst to cover 1.5x spikes.
- Suggested commit term: 12 months for a 15% step discount on list reserved pricing (+ additional 5% if you commit to model quantization and accept up to 8k context trimming policy).

Sizing rationale (high level):
- Baseline throughput mapping: we measured ~16–20 TTS (tokens/sec) per H100 when serving the LLM family you tested with 8-bit quant. That maps to ~700–850 short-response requests/min on typical median prompt/response sizes, assuming our continuous batching and 40ms per-token kernel on average.
- Long-context factor: requests >=8k tokens increase effective token load by ~6x per-request for KV management; we provisioned extra headroom to keep p99 latency in Band A.
- Concurrency: your 380 concurrent sessions translates to roughly 1.2x the peak request rate because many sessions are idle between turns; our estimator uses a 0.6 active-turn factor which produced the 8 GPU outcome above.

Billing & burst handling:
- Bursts: short burst buffer is covered by reserved pool warm standby. If bursts exceed buffer for >10 minutes, overflow is billed as metered usage at pay-as-you-go list rates; we can cap monthly overage at X% of commit by agreement.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Ben — can you add the HW variant assumptions and a simple cost table for the two bands?
2) Alex/Priya — confirm target model (quantized) and a willingness to accept an 8k context trim policy for the cost-optimized band.

I attached a one-pager with the calculation spreadsheet (workload_summary.xlsx) and a draft pricing PDF (redwood_pool_pricing_v1.pdf).

—Markus
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramsey <alex.ramsey@sentinel.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput & SLA bands (Sentinel)

Quick additions on hardware, batching assumptions and pricing structure:

Hardware assumptions:
- H100-equivalent assumed (vRAM and sparsity benefits); optional A100 pool reduces nominal price ~12% but increases peak latency p99 by ~10–18% under long-context workload.
- We size to H100-equivalent GPUs; if Sentinel wants to start on A100 we can model a conversion factor and a hybrid pool.

Batching & caching assumptions used in the calc:
- Continuous batching with max batching delay 8ms, average effective batch size 48 tokens for your trace.
- KV cache hit on repeated session turns reduces token-generation load by ~18% after warm-up; we baked a conservative 10% benefit into Band B sizing.

Pricing & discount structure (proposed):
- List reserved price (H100-eq): $X,XXX per GPU / month (list) — see attached pdf.
- 12-month reserved commit: 15% off list.
- Commit + model quantization (8-bit) + telemetry sharing (30-day rolling): additional 5% off reserved price (cumulative).
- SLA banding: Band A (99.5%) carries a 6% premium on the reserved price to account for higher headroom and higher burst guarantees. Band B (95%) is baseline reserved price.
- Overage: metered at list; we offer a safety cap negotiation (recommend 20% monthly cap for enterprise deals).

Action items:
- I'll draft a two-line pricing table for Band A / Band B (baseline monthly cost and effective per-1k-token unit).
- Karthik — please prepare a short clause about burst-cap mechanics and p99 measurement windows for the commercial term.

—Ben
Principal Product Manager, Capacity Pricing

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@sentinel.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — throughput & SLA bands (Sentinel)

Thanks — helpful notes. A few clarifications from our side after running the attached traces in our staging:
- Peak bursts: we measured sustained 7-minute spikes to ~1.6x baseline during simulated marketing campaigns.
- Model: we plan to run an internal fine-tuned variant; willing to quantize to 8-bit but would prefer the option to toggle for specific workloads (tradeoff OK).
- Procurement asks: can you provide a formal quote with both Band A and Band B numbers, and one column that shows the price if we accept the commit + quantization discount?

We are ok to do a 30-day PoC with a 3 GPU pilot (paid) to validate the long-context KV behavior before moving to full commit. If PoC matches throughput assumptions we will proceed to a 12-month commit.

Forwarding our internal procurement note below for reference.

Best,
Priya
VP, Platform — Sentinel

Solid plan. Confirming next steps and owners so procurement can move quickly:

- Ben: finalize the hardware note and include an A100/hybrid footnote.
- Markus (me): I'll schedule a 30-minute commercial review with Sentinel procurement this week and send over the DocuSign envelope once Karthik confirms numbers.

Tentative timelines: quote in 48 hours, procurement review on-call by EOD Wed, and DocuSign within 7 business days following internal approvals.

I'll mark this thread for the deal (SENT-2026-09) and add the HubSpot link in the final quote.

—Markus
